channel.title: Real_time on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Real_time on Best of AI

item.title: AccuWeather
item.description:
AccuWeather provides weather forecasts for locations around the world. Its app and website show current conditions, hourly and 10-day forecasts, radar and satellite maps, and alerts for severe weather. A signature feature is MinuteCast, which predicts when rain or snow will start and stop at your exact location. Longer-range outlooks give a general sense of the weeks ahead, and features such as air quality and pollen cover health-related conditions.

For businesses, AccuWeather sells data and APIs that power weather information in other apps, media, retailers, utilities, and logistics. Meteorologists combine models, observations, and machine learning to produce its forecasts, and the company has developed AI tools for short-term forecasting and for delivering personalized alerts and impact information, such as how weather might affect travel or operations.

item.title: Azure AI Speech
item.description:
Azure AI Speech brings Microsoft’s speech technology into applications. Speech-to-text transcribes audio in real time or from recordings in many languages, with options for custom vocabulary and speaker separation. Text-to-speech offers a large library of neural voices in many languages and styles, with control over tone, speed, and emotion using SSML. Real-time speech translation converts spoken language into another language for captions or voice.

Additional features serve specialized needs. Custom Neural Voice lets approved customers build a branded voice from recorded samples, subject to a restricted-access process to prevent misuse. Voice live and conversational features support building voice agents, and avatar capabilities create talking presenters from text. Container deployments allow running models on premises or at the edge, and the service integrates with Azure OpenAI and other Azure AI tools.

item.title: LiveKit
item.description:
LiveKit started as an open-source WebRTC platform that handles the hard parts of real-time communication: routing audio and video between many participants, scaling to large rooms, and working across web and mobile. Developers use its SDKs to build video conferencing, livestreaming, telehealth, and interactive broadcast features, and can run it on their own servers or use the hosted LiveKit Cloud.

The company became prominent in voice AI. The Agents framework lets developers build agents that listen, think with a language model, and speak back, with low latency, handling details such as turn-taking and interruptions. It supports telephony so agents can answer phone calls, plus plugins for speech recognition, language, and voice providers. LiveKit powers voice features in well-known AI products, which helped establish it as a standard for real-time AI.

item.title: Tavus
item.description:
Tavus builds AI humans. A person records a short sample, and the platform creates a digital replica that can speak a script, so one recording can become thousands of personalized videos with each viewer’s name and details. This suits sales outreach and customer communications.

The company also provides conversational video agents, which see and hear a user and respond in real time with a face and voice, through an API. Use cases include interviews, coaching, and customer service.

item.title: Google Genie
item.description: Genie is a different kind of generative model. Instead of producing a fixed image or video, it creates a world you can explore: describe a scene, and the model generates an environment that responds as you move through it, frame by frame, with the scene staying consistent as you turn around. DeepMind frames world models as a step toward AI that understands how environments behave, with possible uses in games, robotics training, and simulation.

item.title: Claude Docs
item.description:
Claude Docs brings document writing into the chat. Instead of copying an answer from a conversation into another app, you ask Claude to draft a report, memo, or plan, and it appears as a document you can edit beside the conversation. You can revise it by typing changes directly or by asking Claude to rework sections.

Documents are stored in the Artifacts tab, so they are easy to find later and update across sessions. When the draft is ready, it can be exported to common formats such as Word, PDF, Google Docs, or Markdown. The tool handles headings, lists, and tables, and it works with files and context shared in the conversation.

item.title: Whisper
item.description:
Whisper is a speech-to-text model trained on a very large and varied collection of multilingual audio. That training made it unusually robust: it copes with accents, background noise, and technical vocabulary better than many earlier systems, and it works across dozens of languages. It also detects the spoken language automatically, adds punctuation, and can translate speech from other languages into English text.

The model is released as open source with several sizes, from small ones that run on a laptop to large ones that need a good GPU. That openness led to a wide ecosystem: faster versions such as whisper.cpp and faster-whisper, tools that add timestamps and speaker labels, and many apps for transcription, subtitles, and dictation that use it behind the scenes. OpenAI also offers it through its API for people who do not want to host it.

item.title: SwiftAlerts
item.description:
SwiftAlerts gathers market data into a structure that agents can query. Instead of hunting through separate sources, an agent can ask about relationships between trades, holdings, filings, and sentiment, and get connected answers.

The idea fits the rise of AI agents that research and monitor markets. Reliable data is essential, since trading decisions on wrong information lose money, and nothing from such a tool is financial advice.

Independent information is limited, so check data sources, update speed, and terms. SwiftAlerts is free to start. Alternatives include Unusual Whales, Quiver Quantitative, Benzinga, Polygon.io, and Financial Datasets. SwiftAlerts suits developers building market agents, with caution.

item.title: DataStax
item.description:
DataStax grew up around Apache Cassandra, a database designed for large, always-on applications. Its Astra DB service runs Cassandra in the cloud without servers to manage, and adds vector search so developers can store embeddings and find similar items by meaning. That makes it a base for retrieval-augmented generation, recommendations, and chat features.

The company also supports the tools around AI development. Langflow is a visual builder for agent and retrieval workflows, and its data APIs let developers use document or table models. Pairing a scalable database with AI tools gives teams a path from prototype to large production workloads.

item.title: Pearl
item.description:
Pearl focuses on dental radiograph analysis. Dentists upload X-rays, and the Second Opinion tool highlights suspected problems, such as caries, calculus, and periapical lesions, in real time, which helps catch issues and show patients the findings.

The company has expanded into other uses, including claims review for insurers and tools for dental service organizations that want consistent standards across offices. It holds regulatory clearances for several of its functions.

Pearl is sold on subscription to practices and organizations. AI findings need dentist confirmation, and insurers using AI on claims draw scrutiny. Alternatives include Overjet, VideaHealth, Denti.AI, Dentrix Detect, and Align’s tools. Pearl suits dental practices adding AI radiograph review.

item.title: Alchemy
item.description:
Alchemy gives developers a reliable way to talk to blockchains. Running your own Ethereum node takes expertise and hardware, so most teams rent access instead. Alchemy offers that through APIs that read data, send transactions, and subscribe to events, supporting Ethereum and many other networks, including layer 2 chains. Its infrastructure is built for uptime and speed, which matters when an app depends on real-time chain data.

On top of raw node access are higher-level tools. Enhanced APIs return token balances, NFT metadata, transaction history, and transfers in a form that is easier to use than raw blockchain data. Smart wallet and account abstraction tools let apps create wallets and sponsor gas fees for users, rollup services help teams launch their own chains, and webhooks and subgraphs deliver data to applications. Dashboards show request volume, errors, and latency.

item.title: Character Creator
item.description: Character Creator lets artists build 3D characters without modeling every detail. You start with a base body, adjust shape sliders for face and body, and apply skin, hair, clothing, and accessories from a library. A rigged skeleton and facial controls come ready to animate, so a character can be used right away in games, films, and animations. Pipelines to Unreal Engine, Unity, Blender, Maya, and other tools make it practical in production.

item.title: Creately
item.description:
Creately combines diagramming and whiteboarding in one workspace. You can draw flowcharts, org charts, mind maps, UML diagrams, process maps, wireframes, and more using shape libraries and templates, then connect them with smart connectors that stay attached when you move things. An infinite canvas supports brainstorming and planning, and teams can edit together in real time with comments and cursors.

Some features go beyond plain drawing. Diagrams can be linked to data, so a shape can show information from a spreadsheet or tool, and cards and tables let you build lightweight planning boards. AI features generate a diagram from a text description, summarize or expand notes, and suggest ideas for brainstorming. Presentations and exports in common formats help you share work, and integrations connect with Slack, Confluence, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Teams.

item.title: Moralis
item.description:
Moralis provides ready-made APIs for blockchain data. Instead of reading raw blocks, developers can ask for a wallet’s token balances, NFT holdings, transaction history, or prices and receive clean results across multiple chains, such as Ethereum, Polygon, Solana, and others. This cuts down the time to build wallets, portfolio trackers, NFT marketplaces, and analytics tools.

Other products support app development. Authentication lets users sign in with their wallets, Streams delivers real-time notifications about on-chain events, and node access and data APIs support decentralized finance and gaming projects. Documentation and SDKs help developers integrate quickly, and the platform handles indexing and scaling.

item.title: Sentry
item.description:
Sentry tells developers when their code breaks and why. By adding an SDK to an app, errors are reported with stack traces, the environment, the user’s actions leading up to the problem, and the release that introduced it. Sentry groups duplicate errors into single issues, sends alerts, and links to the relevant commit, so teams can fix a bug quickly rather than discovering it from user complaints.

Beyond error tracking, Sentry monitors performance with tracing that shows slow requests and database queries, and session replay records what the user saw. Cron monitoring watches scheduled jobs, and release health tracks crash-free sessions. Its AI assistant, Seer, analyzes issues to suggest root causes and can propose fixes, and tools for monitoring AI applications trace model calls. It supports most languages and frameworks, and integrates with GitHub, Slack, and Jira.

item.title: Sight Machine
item.description:
Sight Machine tackles the data mess inside factories. Machines, sensors, and systems produce data in many formats, and plants often cannot easily combine it. Sight Machine’s platform pulls in data from equipment, quality systems, and enterprise software, standardizes it into a common model of the production process, and creates a digital twin that shows how products move through the plant.

With that foundation, teams can analyze performance. Dashboards track throughput, yield, scrap, and downtime across lines and sites, machine learning finds the factors that drive defects or slowdowns, and alerts flag issues in near real time. An AI assistant lets operators and engineers ask questions about production data in plain language, and the platform supports sustainability tracking such as energy use.

item.title: Stats Perform
item.description:
Stats Perform collects detailed data about professional sports. Trained collectors and tracking technology record events in matches, such as passes, shots, and player positions, and the company supplies that information to broadcasters, media companies, sportsbooks, leagues, and clubs. Its Opta brand is widely seen in football statistics on television and websites. The data feeds power live scores, fantasy games, and graphics.

AI is used both to create data and to analyze it. Computer vision extracts player and ball tracking from video, which reduces the manual work of collecting information, and models predict outcomes, evaluate player performance, and estimate the value of actions on the field. Coaches and analysts use the tools for scouting and tactical analysis, while media and betting clients use predictions and content such as automated match summaries.

item.title: Whistle
item.description:
Whistle sold small GPS devices that attached to a pet’s collar and reported location through cellular networks. Owners could set safe zones, get an alert when a pet left them, and view recent routes. The devices also tracked activity, rest, and behaviors such as scratching and licking, and the app compared these against typical patterns to point out possible health changes.

The company was owned by Mars Petcare before Tractive, an Austrian pet tracking company, took over the brand. Rather than run two competing platforms, Tractive shut down the Whistle service, and the trackers no longer work. Tractive offered affected customers a replacement device, so owners are generally pointed to its products.

item.title: Wingman
item.description:
Wingman positions itself as a coach for dating apps. A user shares their profile or chat, and the AI suggests better photos, rewrites the bio, and proposes replies to messages. The aim is to help people present themselves well and keep conversations going.

AI-written messages raise authenticity questions, since the person on the other end expects to talk to you. Many users prefer feedback and ideas to full ghostwriting. Sharing screenshots of chats involves other people’s messages, so consider privacy.

item.title: 15Five
item.description:
15Five helps organizations manage how people work and develop. Employees submit short weekly check-ins about priorities, progress, and morale, and managers review them and respond, which keeps a regular rhythm of communication. The platform includes performance reviews, goal and OKR tracking, one-on-one meeting agendas, recognition features, and engagement surveys to measure how employees feel.

AI is used to support managers. The system can summarize check-in responses and survey results, suggest coaching tips, help write review feedback, and flag potential issues like declining engagement or flight risk. Its Best-Self Management framework offers training for managers on developing teams. Reports give HR leaders a view of trends across teams.

item.title: Ahrefs
item.description: Ahrefs is best known for its backlink data. Its crawler maps links across the web, so you can look at any site and see who links to it, which pages draw the most traffic, and what keywords bring visitors. Site Explorer is the tool most people open first, and it is often used to study a competitor’s strategy. Keywords Explorer suggests search terms and estimates how hard each one would be to rank for.

item.title: Aidoc
item.description:
Aidoc builds AI for radiology workflows. When a scan such as a head CT or chest CT is taken, Aidoc’s algorithms analyze it in the background and, if they detect a suspected critical finding, move the study to the top of the radiologist’s worklist and notify the relevant team. This shortens the time to review urgent cases like intracranial hemorrhage, pulmonary embolism, and aortic dissection, where minutes matter.

The company has grown from single-finding triage into a broader platform. It offers an operating system for deploying many algorithms, including those from other developers, and coordinates care for conditions that need multidisciplinary response. Recent work includes foundation models for imaging and tools that combine imaging with clinical data, and a growing number of FDA clearances.

item.title: Amazon CodeWhisperer
item.description:
CodeWhisperer was Amazon’s first coding assistant, a counterpart to GitHub Copilot that suggested lines and whole functions as you typed in editors such as VS Code and the JetBrains IDEs. It was trained with a special focus on AWS APIs, so it was particularly good at code that called S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, and other AWS services. It also supported many popular programming languages.

Two features set it apart from early rivals. A reference tracker flagged suggestions that resembled open-source code and showed the license, and a security scan checked your code for vulnerabilities such as exposed credentials and injection flaws. An individual tier was free, and a professional tier added admin controls and higher limits.

item.title: Apple Maps
item.description: Apple Maps comes installed on every Apple device and has improved a great deal since its rocky start. It provides turn-by-turn driving directions, walking, cycling, and public transit routes, plus lane guidance and speed limit information. Features such as Look Around give a street-level view of many cities, detailed maps show buildings and landmarks in 3D, and downloadable offline maps work without a connection. Guides collect recommended places in a city, and you can share your arrival time with friends.

item.title: Balto
item.description:
Balto sits beside an agent during a call. The software listens to the conversation, recognizes where it is in a script or process, and shows prompts on the agent’s screen: a question to ask, a compliance statement to read, a way to answer an objection. The aim is consistent performance across a team and less reliance on memory.

Supervisors benefit as well. Balto scores calls automatically, shows which behaviors lead to better outcomes, and reduces the number of calls reviewers must listen to by hand. New agents can ramp faster because the software coaches them in real time. Industries with strict rules, such as insurance and financial services, use it for compliance.

item.title: Bing Chat
item.description: Bing Chat was Microsoft’s first big move into AI-assisted search. It put a conversational assistant next to the Bing search box, so you could ask a question and get a written answer with links to sources instead of scanning a page of results. Microsoft later renamed and expanded it as Copilot, and the assistant now works across the web, in the Edge browser, in Windows, and in standalone mobile and desktop apps.

item.title: Blackbox AI
item.description: Blackbox AI was built for programmers. It offers code completion, a chat interface for coding questions, code search, and the ability to turn a screenshot or image into code. A VS Code extension and a web app made it easy to try, and the free tier helped it reach a large number of developers. Users ask it to explain unfamiliar code, convert code between languages, write functions, and fix errors.

item.title: Brandwatch
item.description:
Brandwatch is used by marketing, communications, and research teams to understand what people say online. It collects posts and mentions from social networks, news sites, forums, blogs, and reviews, and lets analysts build searches to track a brand, a competitor, a campaign, or a topic. Dashboards show volume over time, sentiment, demographics, top influencers, and emerging themes, which helps with campaign measurement, crisis monitoring, and product feedback.

AI plays a role in making sense of the data. Language models classify sentiment and topics, group conversations into themes, summarize large sets of posts, and answer questions about the findings in natural language. Image recognition finds logos in pictures posted without any text. Alerts warn teams when mentions spike, and the social management side supports publishing and responding to messages from one place.

item.title: Cartesia
item.description:
Cartesia focuses on speed in voice AI. Its Sonic models, built on state-space model architectures instead of only transformers, generate natural-sounding speech with very low latency, so a voice agent can start speaking almost as soon as a response is ready. That matters for phone calls and live assistants, where delays feel awkward. The company also offers voice cloning and control over emotion and speaking rate.

The platform has grown into a set of real-time voice building blocks. Sonic handles text-to-speech, Ink handles speech-to-text, and tools for managed voice agents help companies deploy agents that answer phone calls. Developers connect through APIs and SDKs, and Cartesia works with common voice agent frameworks and telephony providers. Multilingual support lets one system serve customers in different languages.

item.title: Cerebras
item.description:
Cerebras took an unusual approach to AI hardware. Instead of cutting a silicon wafer into many small chips, it builds a single enormous chip from the whole wafer, which holds an enormous amount of compute and on-chip memory. That design reduces the data movement between chips that slows down large models, and lets it generate tokens at very high speeds.

The company sells its systems and operates a cloud inference service where developers call open models through an API, with fast responses that suit agents, coding tools, and real-time applications. It has partnerships with AI labs and cloud providers, and supports training as well as inference. Developers can try the API with a free tier and then pay by usage, often at competitive per-token rates.

item.title: ClimaCell
item.description:
Tomorrow.io focuses on weather as a business input. Companies in aviation, logistics, energy, retail, and sports use its platform to get forecasts and alerts tailored to their locations and operations, such as a warning when wind will halt crane operations or when snow will affect deliveries. The goal is to turn weather into decisions, not just data.

It builds its own data sources. The company has launched satellites carrying radar to observe precipitation, which supplements ground sensors and models and helps in regions with limited coverage. AI blends these inputs to make short-range forecasts, and an assistant helps users create alerts and ask questions about conditions. APIs deliver the data into other applications.

item.title: Codeium
item.description: Codeium started as a free alternative to GitHub Copilot, offering code completion and chat in more than 40 editors, among them VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Vim, and Neovim. Its free individual tier and wide editor support earned it a large user base among developers who did not want to pay for a coding assistant or switch editors. It added features such as natural-language code search, in-editor chat, and support for dozens of programming languages.

item.title: Codiga
item.description:
Codiga offered real-time code analysis inside the editor. Its plugins for VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and other tools scanned code as you typed for security vulnerabilities, bugs, and violations of coding standards, and a rules engine let teams write their own checks. It also provided a code snippet assistant and, later, AI-based suggestions, and integrated with Git platforms to review pull requests automatically.

The company was acquired by Datadog, which wanted to bring code analysis into its observability and security platform. Codiga’s standalone products were shut down shortly afterward, with refunds for paid subscribers, and the team joined Datadog. The static analysis engine and its rules now underpin Datadog Code Security, and the analyzer is available as open source.

item.title: Dark Sky
item.description:
Dark Sky changed expectations for weather apps. Using radar data and machine learning, it predicted when rain or snow would start and stop at your exact location, with messages such as light rain starting in 10 minutes. That focus on the next hour, rather than a general daily forecast, made it popular with people who walk, run, or commute, and its design was clean and quick to read.

It also offered an API that thousands of apps and websites used for weather data. Developers valued its simple interface and detailed forecasts, which made it a common building block in other products. Apple acquired the company, integrated its technology into Apple Weather, and then retired the Dark Sky app and its API.

item.title: Domo AI
item.description:
Domo aims to put an organization’s data in one place. It connects to hundreds of sources, from databases and spreadsheets to marketing and finance platforms, and lets users clean and combine data and then build dashboards and reports. Business users can view metrics on the web or mobile and set alerts, and developers can build custom apps on top of the data.

AI is built through the product. Users can ask questions in natural language and receive charts and answers, models can forecast and detect anomalies, and AI agents and workflows can automate tasks, such as summarizing reports or triggering actions when numbers change. Domo also lets companies connect their own models, and offers governance features for data access.

item.title: Expensify
item.description:
Expensify is known for making expense reports less painful. Employees photograph receipts or forward them by email, SmartScan extracts the merchant, date, and amount, and the app builds a report for submission. Managers approve in the app, and approved expenses sync to accounting software.

Other features cover company spending. The Expensify Card gives employees corporate cards with real-time receipts matching, policies flag out-of-bounds expenses automatically, and mileage tracking and per diems handle travel. AI helps categorize spending and spot policy issues.

item.title: Fellow
item.description:
Fellow helps teams run better meetings. Before a meeting, it provides shared agendas and templates for one-on-ones, team meetings, and client calls. During the meeting, an AI notetaker records and transcribes, capturing decisions and action items automatically. Afterward, summaries and tasks are sent to attendees.

The platform keeps a record of conversations over time, which suits managers who run recurring one-on-ones. Integrations connect with calendars, Slack, Zoom, Teams, and project tools. AI features answer questions across past meetings and draft follow-up messages. Feedback tools support regular check-ins and performance conversations.

item.title: Freepik AI
item.description: Freepik began as a stock site for vectors, photos, and icons, and many designers already knew it. It has added a full AI suite on top. The image generator creates pictures from text prompts, and tools for editing, upscaling, retouching, and expanding images let users refine them. Video generation and animation features turn stills or prompts into short clips, and a workspace organizes projects and lets you mix different tools.

item.title: Gemini
item.description: Gemini is Google’s family of AI models and the assistant built on top of them. You can use it in the standalone Gemini app and website, but it also shows up inside the products many people already use: it can help draft emails in Gmail, rewrite text in Docs, summarize files in Drive, and answer questions on Android phones. If most of your work and personal life already runs on a Google account, that integration is the main reason to choose Gemini over another assistant.

item.title: Gemini in Workspace
item.description:
Gemini in Workspace brings Google’s models into the apps people use at work. In Gmail, it drafts replies and summarizes long threads. In Docs, it writes, rewrites, and proofreads, and can pull in information from files and email. In Sheets, it helps create formulas, tables, and analysis. In Slides, it generates slides and images, and in Meet it takes notes and summarizes.

A side panel gives a chat assistant that can search across a user’s Drive, Gmail, and Calendar, and answer questions using that content. Organizations can control access, and Google states that business data is not used to train models without permission. Newer features include agents and tools such as NotebookLM for deeper source work.

item.title: Google Maps
item.description: Google Maps is the default map for much of the world. It provides turn-by-turn navigation with live traffic and rerouting, public transit schedules, walking and cycling directions, and detailed maps with business hours, photos, reviews, and popular times. Street View lets you look at places at ground level, Live View uses your phone’s camera to show directions as arrows in the real world, and offline maps work without a connection.

item.title: Google Translate
item.description: Google Translate is the translation tool most people try first. You type or paste text and get a translation in a second, with the language detected automatically. The mobile app adds the features travelers rely on: a camera mode that replaces text on signs and menus, a conversation mode that translates both sides of a spoken exchange, handwriting input, and offline language packs that work without a connection. Chrome can translate whole web pages, and you can upload documents and get a translated copy.

item.title: Groq
item.description: Groq is known for speed. Its chips, called Language Processing Units, were designed from scratch for running AI models rather than adapted from graphics hardware, and they produce text far faster than typical GPU-based services. That makes a difference for chat that feels instant, voice assistants that cannot afford to wait, and agents that make many model calls in a row. The company is not a model lab; it hosts models made by others.

item.title: INK Editor
item.description:
INK combines an editor with optimization guidance. As you write an article, the tool analyzes the search results for your target keyword and gives a score that reflects how well you cover the topic, which terms to include, and how readable the piece is. Suggestions appear in the sidebar, so you can improve the draft while writing instead of editing afterward.

AI features generate text and help overcome writer’s block. You can ask for outlines, introductions, and rewritten paragraphs, and use a plagiarism checker and content shield tools to monitor originality. The product works in a web editor and has extensions for common platforms, and teams can collaborate on content.

item.title: Koala AI
item.description: Koala focuses on creating articles that are designed to rank. You enter a keyword, and the tool analyzes current search results, collects information from the web, and writes a structured article with headings, optional images, and links. It supports one-click generation of long pieces, and special modes for product reviews, listicles, and how-to guides. Real-time data is meant to keep information fresh compared with models that only use training data.

item.title: Lensa AI
item.description:
Lensa is a mobile photo editor best known for a single viral feature. Magic Avatars let users upload a set of selfies and receive a collection of stylized portraits in the style of fantasy art, anime, or illustration. The effect spread quickly on social media, driving downloads and making many people aware of AI image generation. The avatars are created with a model fine-tuned on each user’s photos.

The core of the app is a selfie and portrait editor. It offers retouching for skin and eyes, background replacement, blur and sharpening, and a range of filters and effects. Subscribers get access to the full tool set, and Magic Avatars can be purchased as packs. Prisma Labs, the developer, also makes other photo and AI apps.

item.title: LongShot AI
item.description:
LongShot AI is aimed at publishers and marketers who want blog posts with fewer unsupported claims. You provide a topic or keyword, and the tool researches the web and writes a structured article, with options to cite sources and run fact checks against search results. It can generate outlines, intros, and full drafts, and has a workspace for editing.

Additional features help with the content workflow. An SEO assistant suggests keywords and optimization steps, a rewrite tool paraphrases and adjusts tone, and a calendar helps plan publishing. Teams can collaborate in the editor, and templates cover common formats such as product reviews, how-to articles, and listicles. Users range from solo bloggers to small agencies.

item.title: Mosaic
item.description:
Mosaic is aimed at finance teams that want a modern view of the business. It pulls data from accounting systems, sales tools, and HR platforms into a single model, so metrics like revenue, headcount, and cash are current and consistent. Teams build reports and board decks from live data.

Forecasting and scenario tools let teams test assumptions, such as hiring plans or pricing changes, and see the impact. AI allows users to ask questions in plain language and get analysis, and automates routine commentary and variance explanations.

item.title: Notta
item.description: Notta turns speech into text for people who sit through many conversations. You can record in the mobile or web app, upload audio and video files, or let its assistant join Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams calls. The transcript appears in the app with speaker labels and timestamps, and you can search it, edit it, and share it. It supports a large number of languages, which suits international teams, journalists, and researchers.

item.title: Observe.AI
item.description:
Observe.AI is built for contact centers that handle huge numbers of customer interactions. Quality teams traditionally review a small sample of calls by hand. Observe.AI transcribes and scores all interactions automatically against a company’s quality and compliance criteria, flags issues such as missed disclosures or poor handling of angry customers, and surfaces trends across thousands of conversations.

It also supports agents during and after the call. Real-time guidance suggests what to say or reminds an agent of a required step, and post-call summaries cut the time spent on notes. Coaching tools turn scores into specific feedback for each agent, and dashboards help supervisors see which skills to work on. The platform has added AI agents that speak with customers directly for routine requests, handing off to humans when needed.

item.title: OpenAI Realtime API
item.description:
The Realtime API changes how voice applications are built. Older systems chained speech recognition, a language model, and speech synthesis, adding delay at each step. The Realtime API handles audio in and audio out directly in one model, so responses start sooner and can include tone, pauses, and interruptions that sound natural.

Developers connect over WebRTC or WebSockets to stream audio and receive speech, text, and tool calls. It supports function calling, so a voice agent can look up data or take actions, and it can be used for phone agents, in-app assistants, and language practice.

item.title: Oracle SCM
item.description:
Oracle SCM Cloud brings the functions of a supply chain together in one cloud application suite. It covers planning demand and supply, buying from suppliers, managing inventory and warehouses, running manufacturing, handling orders and fulfillment, and moving goods through transportation and global trade, with product lifecycle management for design data. Because it shares data with Oracle’s finance and HR applications, companies can connect supply chain decisions to financial outcomes.

AI and analytics support the suite. Machine learning improves demand forecasts and supply plans, predictive models flag delays and quality risks, and generative AI assistants help users find information and complete tasks. Oracle has been adding AI agents that can handle routine actions across processes. The suite is delivered in the cloud and updated regularly.

item.title: Perplexity AI
item.description:
Perplexity positions itself as an alternative to the list of links. You ask a question in natural language, it searches the web in real time, reads the pages, and writes a concise answer with citations to each source. That format is helpful for questions where you want a quick overview with a way to check the evidence, such as product comparisons, news, how-to questions, and research basics.

The experience supports continued exploration. Follow-up questions build on earlier context, and focus options narrow the search to categories such as academic sources or discussion forums. Pro Search runs more steps for complex questions, and Deep Research generates longer reports. The Comet browser brings the assistant into everyday browsing, and Spaces organize related research. Users can choose among several models in paid plans.

item.title: Perplexity Sonar
item.description:
Sonar lets developers build apps that answer questions using current web information. Instead of relying only on a model’s training data, a request to Sonar searches the web, reads relevant pages, and returns a response with citations. That grounding is useful for assistants, research tools, news summaries, and any product where freshness and sources matter.

There are several variants. The standard Sonar models are fast and low-cost, Sonar Pro handles more complex queries with more sources, Sonar Reasoning adds step-by-step analysis, and Sonar Deep Research runs multi-step research jobs and writes longer reports. A Search API offers ranked web results for developers who want to feed content to their own models. The API follows a format familiar to users of OpenAI’s, so adoption is simple, and options control which domains to search and how recent results should be.

item.title: Pitch
item.description:
Pitch aims to make presentations that look good without wrestling with layouts. It provides modern templates, smart slide types, and a brand-aware design system that keeps a team’s decks consistent. Collaboration works like a shared document: several people edit at once, leave comments, and track versions, which suits startups, agencies, and sales teams that produce decks together.

Distinctive features include presentation analytics and sharing. You can send a deck as a link and see who viewed it and for how long, which is helpful for investor and sales decks, and recordings let you narrate a deck for asynchronous sharing. AI tools generate slide drafts from a prompt, rewrite text, and create visuals, and the platform integrates with tools like Slack, HubSpot, and Google Drive.

item.title: Redfin
item.description:
Redfin helped modernize home search. Its site and app show listings with details, photos, and maps, along with estimated home values, price history, and tools to compare neighborhoods. A key difference from traditional brokerages is that its agents are salaried employees instead of paid mostly on commission, and Redfin has competed on lower listing fees and a customer-focused model.

Technology plays a large role. Its valuation model, the Redfin Estimate, uses machine learning on recent sales and listing data to estimate home values, and tools offer alerts, tours scheduling, and offers online. AI features help with search and recommendations. Rocket Companies, the owner of Rocket Mortgage, acquired Redfin, bringing mortgage and agent services together under a combined offering, including financing incentives when buyers use both.

item.title: Replica Studios
item.description:
Replica Studios was an Australian startup that made AI voices aimed at creative productions. Its library offered voices of professional actors who had agreed to license their performances, and its tools let game developers and filmmakers generate dialogue with emotion and style. Integrations for game engines such as Unreal and Unity made it easy to put placeholder or final voices into a project, and it also supported voice conversion.

The company drew attention for working with actors instead of against them. It signed an agreement with the actors’ union SAG-AFTRA on terms for licensing digital voice replicas in games, which some actors welcomed and others criticized as inadequate. That debate was part of a wider fight over how AI voices should be used in entertainment, which continues.

item.title: Resemble AI
item.description: Resemble AI builds voices for products and productions. You provide recordings of a speaker, with consent, and the platform trains a voice model that can read any text in that voice, or convert one person’s speech into another voice in real time. Companies use it for branded voices, localization, games, call centers, and media. An API makes it possible to generate speech in applications, and the system supports multiple languages and emotional control.

item.title: Rezi
item.description:
Rezi focuses on a specific worry: that automated screening software will reject a resume before a person reads it. The builder uses a simple, single-column layout and standard section names that parsing software reads reliably. As you write, a score shows how well the resume matches ATS best practices, with checks on length, formatting, action verbs, and keywords from a target job posting.

AI helps with content. It can generate bullet points from a role and tasks, rewrite weak phrases into stronger ones, and tailor a resume to a job description. It also drafts cover letters and has features for tracking applications and tuning your LinkedIn profile. The interface is plain, with less design flair than many competitors, which is intentional.

item.title: Rive
item.description: Rive aims to make animation behave like part of an app. In its editor, designers draw vector shapes, rig them with bones, and animate them on a timeline. The key difference from video or GIF is the state machine: animations can have states and transitions that react to inputs, such as a button being pressed, a character getting closer, or a progress value changing. This lets one asset handle many behaviors.

item.title: Sonix
item.description:
Sonix focuses on fast, accurate machine transcription with a polished editor. You upload a file or connect a source, and get a transcript with timestamps and speaker labels, which you can edit while listening and the text highlights as the audio plays. It supports over forty languages and can translate transcripts into many more. Journalists, researchers, podcasters, and video producers use it to turn recordings into searchable text.

Additional tools support publishing. Sonix exports subtitles and captions in standard formats, offers a media player that embeds the transcript, and provides search across all your files. Integrations and an API connect it with video editors like Premiere Pro and Final Cut, and Zoom. Teams can share folders and custom vocabulary to improve accuracy on specialized terms.

item.title: Spline
item.description:
Spline brings 3D to web designers. In a browser editor that feels more like Figma than Blender, you create shapes, materials, lighting, and animations, then add interactions such as hover effects and clicks. Scenes can be published as links, embedded in websites, or exported to code, and they run in real time in the browser. It’s used for product landing pages, interactive hero sections, games, and design prototypes.

Collaboration and AI features set it apart from traditional 3D tools. Multiple people can edit a scene at once with comments and version history. AI tools can generate 3D objects and textures from text, help with animation, and create scenes from prompts. Physics, particles, and state-based interactions add depth, and integrations with Figma let designers bring in 2D elements.

item.title: Surfer SEO
item.description: Surfer helps writers create content that matches what already ranks. You enter a keyword and it analyzes the top search results, then suggests the terms, headings, length, and structure those pages share. As you write in its editor, a content score updates, giving a quick sense of how well your page covers the topic. Writers and SEO teams use it to guide drafts and to update old posts that have dropped in rankings.

item.title: Talkdesk
item.description:
Talkdesk provides the software contact centers use to handle calls and messages. Customers reach an agent by phone, chat, or messaging, and the platform routes them, records interactions, and reports on performance. Cloud delivery makes setup quicker than legacy systems.

AI is part of each layer. Virtual agents resolve common requests, agent assist suggests replies and surfaces knowledge during calls, quality tools score conversations automatically, and forecasting helps schedule staff. Industry versions serve healthcare, financial services, and retail.

item.title: Voicemod
item.description: Voicemod changes how you sound as you speak. You choose a voice effect, such as a robot, a deep voice, or a character, and the app processes your microphone audio in real time. It works as a virtual microphone, so apps like Discord, Zoom, OBS, and many games treat it like a normal mic. Gamers and streamers use it for fun and for roleplay, and some people use it for privacy.

item.title: Weather.ai
item.description:
Weather.ai positions itself as a forecast service built on machine learning rather than only traditional physics models. It aims to give hourly and daily forecasts for specific locations, which is the kind of hyperlocal output people want for planning a run, a trip, or an event. The site focuses on readable forecasts, and an API is available for developers.

Machine learning is now common in weather prediction. Large research efforts from Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, and others have shown that models trained on decades of observations can produce competitive forecasts quickly, and many startups sell tailored predictions built on this work. Services in this space usually combine public data from national weather agencies with their own models and corrections.

item.title: WeatherBug
item.description:
WeatherBug built its name on a dense network of weather stations, often at schools and other local sites. That gives it temperature, wind, and rain readings from places closer to you than a distant airport sensor, which helps when conditions change quickly, such as during a storm. The app combines that observation data with forecast models for hourly and multi-day outlooks.

Its mobile app is the main product. Users get radar maps, lightning detection, and alerts for severe weather and rainfall, along with air quality and pollen information in some regions. A subscription removes ads and unlocks extra features, and some of the forecasting uses machine learning to adjust model output for local conditions.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description:
Writesonic started as a template-based copywriter and has widened into a content and marketing suite. Users pick a tool for blog articles, ad copy, product descriptions, emails, or social posts, give a brief, and get a draft. A long-form article writer can produce SEO-minded posts from a keyword with outlines and sources, and a chat assistant answers questions and drafts on demand.

Recent additions center on search visibility. Writesonic has tools to see how a brand is mentioned in AI answer engines such as ChatGPT and Perplexity, plus recommendations for improving content. It also offers brand voice settings, an editor with SEO scoring, and integrations with WordPress and other platforms.

item.title: Writesonic
item.description: Writesonic began as a template-driven AI writer for marketing copy. You choose a type of content, such as a blog post, ad, product description, or social caption, fill in some details, and get a draft. A longer-form article writer builds full posts with an outline, headings, and optional SEO guidance, and a chat assistant answers questions and can search the web. A browser extension and integrations with WordPress and other tools help get content published.

item.title: Zed AI
item.description:
Zed is built for speed. Its editor, written in Rust, starts quickly and stays responsive on large projects, and multiplayer editing lets several people work in the same file with voice and chat.

AI is built in rather than added by extension. Users chat with models in an assistant panel, ask for inline edits, and run an agent that edits code across files, with support for several providers and local models. Edit predictions suggest the next change as you type, and the Agent Client Protocol lets other agents run inside.

item.title: Zeni
item.description:
Zeni provides outsourced finance for startups. Companies connect their bank accounts, and Zeni handles bookkeeping, accounts payable, tax, and CFO services, with a dashboard showing cash, burn, and runway in real time. Humans check the AI’s work.

The service replaces a part-time accountant or finance hire for early-stage companies. Monthly reports help founders and investors understand the business.

Zeni is a subscription service. Alternatives include Pilot, Bench, Puzzle, Digits, and a traditional accountant. Zeni suits startups wanting outsourced finance.

item.title: Zety
item.description: Zety walks job seekers through making a resume. You choose a template, answer prompts about your experience and education, and see a preview that updates as you type. The builder suggests wording for job duties and skills, which is helpful if you struggle with the phrasing, and it formats everything cleanly for PDF or Word download. It also builds cover letters and offers a library of guides and examples for different industries.

item.title: Arize AI
item.description:
Arize helps teams see what their models are doing after deployment. For classic machine learning, it tracks performance, detects when input data drifts away from training data, and helps identify which segments of users a model is failing. Alerts point teams to problems before they affect the business.

For LLM applications, it traces each request through the chain of prompts, retrieval, and tool calls, and runs evaluations that score responses for relevance, hallucination, and safety. This helps developers find why an answer was wrong and test fixes. Arize Phoenix, the company’s open-source tool, offers tracing and evaluation that can run locally.

item.title: Brex
item.description:
Brex built a corporate card and spend platform for startups and growing companies. Businesses issue cards to employees with set limits, and expenses are captured and matched automatically, with receipts collected through the app and policies enforced in real time. Finance teams get visibility into spending and can close their books faster than with manual expense reports.

The platform grew into a broader finance system. It includes bill payments, reimbursements, travel booking, banking features, and budgeting, with integrations to accounting software such as NetSuite and QuickBooks. AI agents handle tasks such as filling out expense reports, checking receipts for policy violations, and answering finance questions, aiming to reduce time spent on back-office work.

item.title: CleverTap
item.description:
CleverTap serves brands with mobile apps and large user bases. It collects behavioral data such as app opens, purchases, and feature use, builds segments, and lets marketers send push notifications, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and in-app messages. Journeys can be designed visually so that actions trigger the next message.

AI is used for prediction and optimization. Models estimate which users are likely to churn or convert, choose the best time and channel for each message, and recommend products. A proprietary database designed for large volumes of event data keeps analysis fast, and analytics show retention, funnels, and campaign results.

item.title: Gladia
item.description:
Gladia provides speech-to-text as a service for developers. Companies send audio from calls, meetings, or videos and receive transcripts with timestamps, speaker labels, and optional translation. It handles dozens of languages and can detect which one is being spoken.

Real-time transcription suits live captioning and voice agents, while batch processing handles recordings at scale. Extra features include summaries, sentiment, and named entity detection. The API is aimed at products built on audio, such as meeting assistants, call analytics, and media tools.

item.title: Oliv AI
item.description:
Oliv AI assists sellers before, during, and after calls. Before a meeting, it gathers context on the account and contacts and drafts a briefing. During the call, it records and transcribes. Afterward, it writes notes, updates the CRM, and drafts follow-up emails.

For managers, it scores deals against frameworks such as MEDDIC and highlights risks and gaps, which supports coaching and forecasting. The product presents these functions as agents that take over routine sales admin.

item.title: Prefect
item.description:
Prefect lets developers turn Python functions into reliable workflows. By adding decorators, a script becomes a flow with tasks that retry on failure, run on a schedule, and report state. Teams view runs, logs, and results in a dashboard.

It supports dynamic workflows, concurrency, and deployment to different infrastructure, from a laptop to Kubernetes. A hosted cloud service handles scheduling and observability, and the open-source server can be self-hosted. It is used for data pipelines and machine learning jobs.

item.title: Revenue.io
item.description:
Revenue.io, formerly RingDNA, combines calling with conversation intelligence. During a call, it listens and surfaces prompts, such as a competitor battlecard or the right answer to a pricing objection. After the call, it transcribes, summarizes, and scores conversations against a playbook.

Managers get coaching insights and forecasting signals. The platform includes a dialer and integrates with Salesforce, so call data flows into the CRM. AI assistants draft follow-ups and update records.

item.title: Sapling
item.description:
Sapling helps support and sales teams write faster and more consistently. As an agent types in the help desk or CRM, Sapling suggests completions based on past replies, fixes grammar and tone, and inserts approved snippets. This reduces typing time and variation.

Managers use quality analytics to monitor response times and consistency, and see how suggestions are used. It integrates with Zendesk, Salesforce, Intercom, and other tools, and offers an API and an AI content detector.

item.title: Speechmatics
item.description:
Speechmatics provides speech-to-text as a service. Developers send audio and get transcripts with timestamps, speaker labels, and language detection. The company emphasizes accuracy across accents and dialects, which is an area where many systems show bias.

Products include real-time transcription for live captioning and voice agents, batch processing, translation, and deployment options on premises for sensitive data. Customers include media, contact center, and healthcare companies.

Speechmatics is priced by usage. Alternatives include Deepgram, AssemblyAI, OpenAI Whisper, Gladia, and Google Cloud Speech-to-Text. Speechmatics suits organizations needing accurate multilingual transcription.

item.title: Spike
item.description:
Spike presents email like a chat. Threads become conversations, which can feel faster, and a unified view combines email with notes, tasks, and calendar. Teams can discuss messages privately without forwarding.

AI helps with summaries of long threads, drafting replies, and organizing the inbox, and shared inboxes support small teams. It works with many email providers.

Spike has a free tier and paid plans. Chat-style email is a taste, and some prefer traditional layouts. Alternatives include Superhuman, Shortwave, Hey, Gmail with Gemini, and Front. Spike suits people who want a conversational inbox.

item.title: Transkriptor
item.description:
Transkriptor turns speech into text. Users upload files, record in the app, or connect meeting platforms, and receive a transcript with timestamps and speaker labels that can be edited and exported. Subtitles and translations are supported.

Features include meeting bots that join calls, AI summaries, and a chat assistant to ask questions about a recording. It serves students, journalists, researchers, and businesses.

Transkriptor has a free trial and paid plans by hours. Accuracy depends on audio quality, and sensitive recordings need privacy checks. Alternatives include Otter.ai, Trint, Descript, Fireflies, and Whisper-based tools. Transkriptor suits people transcribing interviews and meetings.

item.title: Trigger.dev
item.description:
Trigger.dev lets developers write long-running work in code. A task defined in TypeScript can run for minutes or hours without hitting serverless time limits, with automatic retries, queues, and scheduling. A dashboard shows runs, logs, and failures.

It is popular for AI workloads such as calling models in sequence, processing documents, and agent workflows that need durable execution. Integrations connect with frameworks like Next.js, and the platform can be self-hosted.

item.title: Trint
item.description:
Trint speeds up working with recordings. Users upload interviews, press conferences, or footage and get transcripts that link to the audio, so editing the text is easy to verify. Teams can search across an archive, highlight quotes, and build stories from selections.

The platform supports many languages, translation, and subtitles, and offers collaboration for newsrooms with permissions and shared workspaces. AI features create summaries and help extract key moments.

Trint is paid, with plans by features and seats. Accuracy depends on audio quality. Alternatives include Otter.ai, Descript, Transkriptor, Verbit, and Rev. Trint suits media teams that work with large volumes of recorded content.

item.title: Verbit
item.description:
Verbit blends machine and human work. AI produces a first draft of the transcript, and professional editors review and correct it, which yields higher accuracy than automatic transcription alone. Services include captioning for live events, court reporting, and transcripts of recorded media.

Education is a big market: universities use Verbit to caption lectures and meet accessibility requirements. Its platform integrates with video tools and learning systems, and the company has acquired several transcription and captioning firms.

item.title: AssemblyAI
item.description:
AssemblyAI is infrastructure for apps that need to understand speech. A developer sends audio from a call, meeting, podcast, or video, and the API returns an accurate transcript with word-level timestamps. It supports pre-recorded files and real-time streaming, so it can power live captions and voice assistants as well as batch transcription. Customers use it to build call analytics, meeting note takers, media search, and compliance tools.

Beyond transcription, a layer of speech understanding turns text into structured data. It can separate speakers, summarize a conversation, detect topics, and score sentiment. Guardrails features redact personal information and filter sensitive content before the data goes anywhere else. An LLM Gateway lets developers pass transcripts to language models for tasks like extracting action items, and a voice agent API supports speech-to-speech applications.

item.title: Clearscope
item.description: Clearscope helps writers produce content that is complete enough to rank. You enter a keyword, and it analyzes the top results to show the terms, topics, and questions that strong pages tend to include. As you draft in its editor, a grade updates, so you can see whether the page covers what searchers expect. Plugins for Google Docs, Word, and WordPress let writers work in familiar tools instead of switching to a separate app.

item.title: Deepgram
item.description:
Deepgram sells speech AI to developers. Its speech-to-text API transcribes audio in real time or from recordings, and it is designed for accuracy at low latency and low cost, which matters for call centers, meeting tools, and voice assistants that process large volumes. Features include speaker labeling, punctuation, keyword boosting, and support for many languages, and models can be customized to a company’s vocabulary.

The platform has widened to cover the whole voice stack. A text-to-speech product generates natural voices with low latency, and a voice agent API combines speech recognition, a language model, and speech synthesis into a single service for building conversational agents that can hold phone calls. Enterprises can run Deepgram in their own cloud or on-premises when data cannot leave their control.

item.title: Grok
item.description: Grok is the chatbot from xAI, Elon Musk’s AI company. It is built into X, so you can ask it about a post, a trending topic, or a thread without leaving the feed, and it is also available as a separate app and at grok.com. Its main distinguishing feature is live access to posts on X, which makes it unusually quick at summarizing what people are saying about a breaking story. The tone is a little looser than other assistants, and it will answer some questions that more cautious tools decline.

item.title: Hedy AI
item.description:
Hedy AI takes a different role from notetakers that summarize afterward. It listens during a call or conversation and shows prompts in the moment: a suggested answer, a question to ask, or a reminder of context. The goal is to help the user perform better while the conversation is happening.

After the meeting, it produces transcripts and summaries and can store notes for future sessions. People use it for sales calls, interviews, negotiations, and learning situations. It can run alongside video calls or in person on a phone or computer.

item.title: Krea AI
item.description:
Krea became popular for its real-time canvas. As you type a prompt or sketch shapes, the image updates almost instantly, which turns generation into a live, exploratory process instead of waiting for each result. That immediacy suits designers and artists who iterate visually, adjusting composition and style through gestures rather than rewriting prompts.

The platform has expanded into a wide creative toolkit. It lets you generate images and video with a selection of models from different providers, upscale and enhance images with a strong emphasis on detail, edit existing pictures, and train custom styles from your own examples. Features such as pattern and logo generation, and tools for animating stills, appeal to designers and motion artists. Multiple models in one place make comparison easy.

item.title: MarketAlerts.ai
item.description:
MarketAlerts.ai watches the market on behalf of its users. Investors list their holdings, and the service monitors news, filings, price moves, and other events, sending alerts when something relevant happens and summarizing why it might matter. Some alerts include AI-generated signals about possible actions.

Such tools save time for people who cannot follow the market all day, but they carry risks. AI-generated trade signals are not reliable predictions, markets are unpredictable, and acting on automated signals can lose money. Nothing here is financial advice.

item.title: Microsoft Copilot
item.description: Microsoft uses the Copilot name for a family of assistants rather than one product. The consumer Copilot app and website work like other AI chatbots: you can ask questions, generate text and images, talk by voice, and have it look at your screen or camera for help with what you are doing. It is built into Windows and the Edge browser, where it can summarize pages, compare information across open tabs, and help with tasks as you browse.

item.title: Pounce
item.description:
Pounce helps with timely engagement. It monitors social platforms for topics and conversations related to a brand or niche, flags those gaining traction, and suggests ways to participate, such as posting a response or creating content.

Social media managers use it to catch trends early, when joining a conversation can earn reach. Faster detection and suggested angles shorten the path from trend to post.

Independent information is limited. Brands should be careful about jumping on trends, as tone-deaf posts cause harm. Pounce has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Brandwatch, Sprout Social listening, Exploding Topics, BuzzSumo, and Google Trends. Pounce suits social managers who want trend alerts.

item.title: Tripo3D
item.description:
Tripo focuses on speed and consistency. Enter a description or upload an image, and it generates a 3D model in seconds to a minute, with options for style and level of detail. The models are meant to be usable in games, animation, 3D printing, and e-commerce, and the platform provides downloads in common formats like GLB, FBX, and OBJ.

Features go beyond the initial generation. Tools can create cleaner topology for animation, generate or replace textures from a prompt, add skeletons so characters can be posed, and apply animations. A segmentation option separates a model into parts for editing. An API and integrations with Blender, Unity, Unreal, and other applications fit it into creative pipelines, and a community library offers starting points.

item.title: Voicetype AI
item.description:
Voicetype AI lets people speak instead of type. A user holds a hotkey, speaks, and the text appears in the active app, with punctuation and formatting handled automatically. It works across email, documents, chat, and code editors.

AI cleans up filler words and false starts, and supports many languages. Custom dictionaries help with names and jargon. Dictation can speed up writing for people who think out loud.

Voicetype AI has a free tier and paid plans. Independent information is limited, so check privacy and where audio is processed. Alternatives include Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, Dragon, Apple dictation, and Talon. Voicetype AI suits people who want voice typing everywhere.

item.title: Zoom AI Companion
item.description: AI Companion is the assistant built into Zoom’s meeting, chat, phone, and document tools. Its most used feature is the meeting summary: it listens to the call, produces a transcript, and writes up the main points and action items, which it can share with attendees right after the meeting ends. If you join late, it can catch you up on what was said. It can also answer questions about a meeting in progress, such as what was decided on a topic a few minutes ago.
